record.paper_title: Problems and Conjectures Presented at the Third International Conference on Permutation Patterns (University of Florida, March 7-11, 2005)
record.context_brief: Existence of growth rates for finitely based classes
record.original_question: If B is a finite set of permutation patterns, does the limit gr(Av(B)) = lim_{n→∞} |Av(B) ∩ S_n|^{1/n} always exist?

evidence.quote: It would be natural to define the growth rate of X as gr(X) = lim n→∞ root_n |X ∩ Sn|, but this limit is not known to exist in general.
Conjecture (Vince Vatter): For any finite set of patterns B, the growth rate of Av(B) exists.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S_n$ denote the set of permutations of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. For permutations $\sigma\in S_n$ and $\pi\in S_k$ with $k\le n$, say that $\sigma$ contains $\pi$ as a pattern if there exist indices $1\le i_1<i_2<\cdots<i_k\le n$ such that the sequence $\sigma(i_1),\sigma(i_2),\dots,\sigma(i_k)$ has the same relative order as $\pi(1),\pi(2),\dots,\pi(k)$; otherwise $\sigma$ avoids $\pi$. For a set $B$ of permutations, let
$$\mathrm{Av}(B)=\{\sigma : \sigma\text{ avoids every pattern in }B\},$$
and write $\mathrm{Av}(B)\cap S_n$ for the permutations in $\mathrm{Av}(B)$ of length $n$. The (upper) growth rate of $\mathrm{Av}(B)$ is
$$\overline{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Av}(B))=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\bigl|\mathrm{Av}(B)\cap S_n\bigr|^{1/n}.$$
By the Marcus–Tardos theorem, this $\limsup$ is finite whenever $B\neq\emptyset$.

Question: Prove or disprove that for every finite set $B$ of permutations the limit
$$\mathrm{gr}(\mathrm{Av}(B))=\lim_{n\to\infty}\bigl|\mathrm{Av}(B)\cap S_n\bigr|^{1/n}$$
exists (as a real number).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on permutation classes (including surveys and the 2019 work of Bevan and others on growth rates up to the uncountability threshold) continues to refer to the existence of the growth rate (Stanley–Wilf limit) for general, and even finitely based, permutation classes as an open conjecture. The Marcus–Tardos theorem establishes finiteness of the upper limit, but existence of the limit itself has not been established in general.

status_evidence.title: Growth Rates of Permutation Classes: From Countable to Uncountable
status_evidence.snippet: It is conjectured that every permutation class has a growth rate; the limit is known to exist for principal classes but it is open whether it exists for all permutation classes.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of the growth rate for general permutation classes (including those with finite basis) is referenced as a still-open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Permutation class - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Although the Stanley–Wilf limit is known to exist for principal classes, it remains a conjecture for arbitrary permutation classes.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of the Stanley–Wilf limit (growth rate) for general permutation classes remains conjectural.
